correctness.rationale: For unit pairs, Dragomir approximate reverse orthogonality is exactly a lower bound on dist(y,Rx). Dihedral symmetry puts x on one vertical octagon edge. At edge-interior points the unique support functional forces y to be vertical, giving distance 1/(1+r|t|). At a vertex the complete support cone is parameterized by q in [0,1]; the two exact norm branches N(q,-1)=1 and (1+q)/sqrt2 yield distance at least 1/(1+r^2) in both cases. The pair x=(1,r), y=(0,-1) is Birkhoff--James orthogonal and attains equality. Substituting r=sqrt2-1 gives d0=(2+sqrt2)/4 and sigma_D=sqrt(1-d0^2)=sqrt((5-2sqrt2)/8).

originality.rationale: The motivating full text was inspected at the definition of D-approximate orthogonality, its global D-symmetry definition, the compactness theorem proving existence of some global parameter in every finite-dimensional Banach space, and the regular-polygon theorem for the distinct C-symmetry relation. No optimal numerical D-parameter is computed there for the regular octagon. Semantic searches covered the exact terminology, the octagon, the radical value, and the equivalent reverse-line-distance formulation. The closest indexed exact D-parameter result is for ell_3^2 and ell_{3/2}^2, not a consequence covering the octagonal norm.

value.rationale: The motivating theorem guarantees a global D-symmetry threshold in every finite-dimensional Banach space but leaves the threshold nonquantitative. The regular octagon is a canonical nonsmooth test space and the exact value turns the existence theorem into a sharp metric statement. The equivalent reverse-line separation identifies the worst Birkhoff asymmetry and its extremal vertex-edge geometry, making the number reusable in comparisons with other quantitative orthogonality invariants.
